Siloxanes are compounds with a silicon-oxygen backbone (Si-O-Si) that typically have organic groups (like methyl, ethyl, or phenyl groups) attached to the silicon atoms. These organic side chains significantly influence the properties of siloxanes.

The organic side chains in siloxanes (particularly methyl groups in common siloxanes like polydimethylsiloxane) confer hydrophobicity to the molecules. This hydrophobic nature is why siloxanes are commonly used in waterproofing applications, as water repellents, and in personal care products.

The hydrophobicity comes from the non-polar nature of the organic groups, which repel water molecules. This is in contrast to the Si-O backbone, which by itself would be more polar and potentially interact with water.
